Modified response: The statement is cautious on growth (“the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity and pose risks”), but it also outlines an aggressive countercyclical response—cutting the federal funds rate to the effective lower bound, launching large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanding repo operations, easing discount-window terms, and coordinating dollar liquidity swap lines. Consistent with the credit view and investment–cash flow evidence (e.g., Oliner and Rudebusch; Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein; Gertler and Gilchrist), these actions should reduce external finance premia and ease credit constraints, supporting investment and employment even amid liquidity stress. With inflation below target and both market- and survey-based expectations little changed, near-term risks skew toward disinflation, aligning with inflation-forecast targeting principles (Svensson) and the long-run money–inflation linkage. Overall tone: negative on the near-term outlook but meaningfully mitigated by decisive policy support.
